name: Pro 2a | Salon WhatsApp Booking Bot | Advanced

parameters.content:
## START HERE
**1.** Run `schema.sql` then `seed.sql` against your Postgres (Supabase / Neon free tier is fine).
**2.** Add ONE Postgres credential and select it on all four Postgres nodes.
**3.** Put your own verify token in **Verify Token**, then in Meta: WhatsApp > Configuration > Edit, callback URL =
the **production** URL of *WhatsApp Message In*, and subscribe to the **messages** field.
**4.** In the `tenants` row set `phone_number_id` and `wa_token` (permanent System User token) for the salon.
**5.** Activate. Test webhooks only reach a workflow while its editor tab is open - this one must be **Active**.

Adding salon #2 = one INSERT into `tenants`. No new workflow, no new nodes.

## How a message becomes a booking
**Read Message** flattens Meta's envelope and builds one query.
**Load Salon + Session** does the whole read in a single round trip:
which salon owns this number, its services, staff, hours, existing
bookings, this customer, and where the conversation had got to.
**Booking Engine** is a state machine - no AI. It works out the free
slots and only ever offers those.
**Run DB Action** is the only thing that decides a booking is real.
Two people tapping 10:30 at the same instant: the database gives it
to one of them, and **Finalize Reply** offers the other the times
that are genuinely still free.

## Owner alert (optional)
WhatsApp only allows free-form messages within 24h of the
customer's last message. The owner has not messaged you,
so their alert must be an **approved template** with
exactly **3 variables**: customer, service, when.

Create it in Meta > WhatsApp Manager > Message templates,
then put its name in `tenants.owner_template` and the
owner's number in `tenants.owner_wa`.
Leave both NULL and this branch simply never fires - new
bookings still appear in the dashboard instantly.
